entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: Supported. The text explicitly states: “the resulting material had a particle size of about 200 nm (Figure 1a)” in the Results/Discussion section describing the SEM image. This directly matches the extracted SEM particle size value (200 nm) and provenance (Figure 1a).

The text explicitly states: “A thin layer of carbon was coated on the surface of Na3MnZr(PO4)3 particles during the synthesis procedure … (Figure 1b).” This supports the TEM-based observation of a thin surface carbon layer, consistent with the extracted value “thin surface layer.”

The text explicitly states: “The crystalline region … exhibited lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of about 0.64 nm, consistent with the (012) atomic planes … (Figure 1c).” This directly supports interplanar spacing (012) = 0.64 nm and matches the alleged provenance (Figure 1c).

Page 2 (Results and Discussion, “Synthesis and Crystal Structure...”) explicitly states: (1) space group “R3̅c” (i.e., R-3c) from Rietveld refinement of the XRD pattern (Figure 1d), and (2) lattice parameters “a = 8.988 Å, and c = 22.594 Å” for Na3MnZr(PO4)3. These match the extracted values and are tied to Figure 1d as alleged provenance.

The paper explicitly states: “the amount of coated carbon was about 7.1% according to thermogravimetric analysis (Figure S1)” in the Results and Discussion section (page 2 of the provided text). This supports the extracted TGA-derived carbon content of 7.1%.

The text explicitly states: “Two oxidation peaks at 3.6 and 4.1 V are revealed in the cyclic voltammetry profiles…” and “The two reduction peaks located at 4.0 and 3.5 V…”, matching the extracted oxidation and reduction peak voltages. This statement appears in the Results/Discussion section adjacent to the mention of Figure 2a, consistent with the alleged provenance.

All extracted galvanostatic charge–discharge metrics are explicitly stated in the paper text associated with Figure 2 (and not only in the figure itself). Specifically: discharge capacity 105 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C; 82 mAh g−1 at 1 C; 52 mAh g−1 at 10 C (page 3, discussion of Figure 2c). Cycling stability: 91% capacity retained after 500 cycles at 0.5 C and average Coulombic efficiency 98.7% (page 3, discussion of Figure 2d). These match the extracted values and units.

The paper explicitly reports Mn 3p XPS binding energies at different states of charge: 48.8 eV before charging (pristine), 49.5 eV after charging to 3.9 V, and 50.2 eV after charging to 4.3 V, referencing Figure S4. These match the extracted values and units exactly.

The paper explicitly reports cycling over 500 charge/discharge cycles: the abstract states the material retains 91% of initial capacity after 500 cycles, and the main text (Electrochemical Performance, Figure 2d description) states “91% of the initial capacity could be retained after 500 cycles at 0.5 C rate.” This supports a cycle life value of 500 cycles.
